newsitem.title: TUNISIA: U.S. aviator on Earhart flight lands in Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aviator on Earhart flight lands in Tunisia.

text.p: U.S. pilot Linda Finch landed in Tunisia on Monday in her attempt to retrace Amelia Earhart's 1937 flight around the world, the official Tunisian agency said.

Finch, a 46-year-old Texan businesswoman, set off from Oakland, California, on March 17 in a 1935 Lockheed Electra 10E, the same model used by Earhart, and also followed a similar route used by the famous aviator.
"During her short visit to Tunisia, Finch is going to visit some historic monuments," the agency said.
Earhart, the first woman to fly alone across the Atlantic, completed 22,000 miles (35,400 km) of her journey and vanished in July 1937 on the leg from New Guinea to Howland Island.
Finch's journey, called "World Flight 1997", will cross five continents and includes more than 30 stops in 20 countries.
She is expected to leave Tunisia on Wednesday morning for Athens, the agency added.
